verdict: Server lane (S1-S4, S7, S8) is sound and the PR #410 duplicate-GET keep-alive is preserved. Client lane (S5, S6, S9) ships a High that re-creates the eviction the product constraint forbids, and its only test is a tautology, so H2 is effectively unverified.

findings.title: clearCredentials() unconditionally wipes localStorage, so a force-login tab evicts the driver's own live Scout session
findings.why: The whole point of S5/S6 is that a tab-scoped force-login session must not touch the driver's localStorage-backed credentials (AC5: coexist, do not evict). clearCredentials() does removeCredential(key) against the resolved store AND then localStorage.removeItem(key) AND sessionStorage.removeItem(key) for all four credential keys, regardless of scope. Both call sites are on the normal, expected path: (a) handleUnauthorized() fires whenever the force token is revoked -- which is exactly what exitAdminMode()/leave() do -- or when the 60-minute TTL lapses; (b) logout() fires if the admin signs out inside the force-login PWA. In either case the driver's live `scanner_token`/`scanner_user`/`scanner_kit` are deleted from the shared origin localStorage, and the driver's own tab bounces to /scout/login on its next poll. This is the same cross-tab identity damage H2 describes, just in the eviction direction, and the new e2e spec's own setup (driver tab on localStorage + force tab on sessionStorage in one context) is precisely the scenario it breaks. The inline comment ('Also clear the other store so a scope flip cannot leave a stale bearer') states the intent, but the sweep is unscoped.
findings.fix_hint: Branch on scope: when isTabScoped(), remove only the sessionStorage credential keys plus the scope marker. Keep the both-store sweep for the non-tab-scoped path (where localStorage is this tab's own store and a leftover sessionStorage bearer really is stale). Add a PHPUnit-independent assertion in the e2e spec that a 401 in the force tab leaves localStorage['scanner_token'] intact.

findings.title: The new Playwright spec is a tautology - it re-implements resolveStorage() inline and never exercises scoutCredentials.js, leaving H2 with zero executable coverage
findings.why: The spec navigates both pages to about:blank, then hand-writes sessionStorage['scout_credential_scope']='tab', sessionStorage['scanner_token'] and sessionStorage['scanner_user'] inside page.evaluate, then re-derives the storage choice in the test body (`const store = scope === 'tab' ? sessionStorage : localStorage`). The application bundle is never loaded, markTabScoped()/setCredential()/getCredential() are never called, and no request is ever issued, so the assertions only prove that sessionStorage is per-tab and localStorage is shared -- facts about the browser, not about this diff. Deleting resources/js/clarity-scout/lib/scoutCredentials.js entirely would leave this test green. The `forceDidNotTouchLocal` expectation is additionally vacuous: it is an `||` chain whose second clause is true by construction given the driver-tab setup. None of the three behaviours plan.md S9 specified are present (tab A still sends driver A's bearer after tab B boots; a reload of tab A keeps driver A; the driver's normal-login tab still rehydrates). With no JS unit runner in the repo (vitest was explicitly out of scope), H1's server half is well covered but H2 -- the headline defect and the one carrying the wrong-driver-data-at-200 risk -- has no verification at all.
findings.fix_hint: Drive the real flow: authenticate via the .test-gated /__qa/login lever, hit /scout/force-login/{kitA} in tab A and /scout/force-login/{kitB} in tab B, then assert from the app's own state (e.g. intercept /api/scout/me and compare the Authorization bearer per tab, or read window state) that tab A still carries driver A after tab B boots, that reloading tab A preserves driver A, and that a separately-logged-in driver tab still rehydrates from localStorage. Add the H1 regression assertion from finding #1 to the same spec.

findings.title: The tab-scope marker is never cleared, so a force-login tab stays tab-scoped for the rest of its life and a later real driver login in it silently cannot rehydrate
findings.why: CREDENTIAL_KEYS covers the four credential keys but not SCOPE_MARKER_KEY, and nothing else removes it. After a force-login tab 401s (fetch.js:74-79) or the admin logs out, the tab is redirected to /scout/login with scout_credential_scope='tab' still set. A normal driver login performed in that same tab then routes every setCredential() write into sessionStorage, so the session evaporates on tab close and never rehydrates on PWA relaunch -- which is the documented reason localStorage was retained ('Normal driver login keeps using localStorage so a PWA relaunch can rehydrate', scoutCredentials.js:4). The failure is completely silent: the app works until the tab is closed. main.js's boot path reads through the same accessor, so it inherits the wrong store too.
findings.fix_hint: Add an explicit clearTabScope() that removes SCOPE_MARKER_KEY, and call it from clearCredentials() (or from the logout/401 paths directly, after the scope-aware credential clear in finding #1). Cover it in the e2e spec: force tab -> 401 -> login as a driver -> assert the bearer landed in localStorage.

findings.title: markTabScoped() fails silently and resolveStorage() then falls back to the shared-localStorage path, reinstating H2 with no signal
findings.why: markTabScoped() swallows any sessionStorage.setItem failure (Safari private browsing, blocked/partitioned storage, quota). isTabScoped() then returns false, resolveStorage() returns localStorage, and forceAuthenticate() writes the gate-bypassing force bearer straight into the driver's shared localStorage slot -- the exact H2 defect, on a code path that reports success. The catch block's comment ('fall through; resolveStorage still prefers sessionStorage when possible') is factually inverted: resolveStorage() prefers localStorage whenever the marker is absent, and the module docblock deliberately rules out a read-through fallback, so there is no compensating guard. Given the force ability bypasses kit, permission and feature checks (ClarityScoutMiddleware:25, routes/channels.php:30), the failure mode is mismatched requests returning 200 with another driver's data.
findings.fix_hint: Have markTabScoped() verify the write and return a boolean (set then read back). In forceAuthenticate(), if tab scoping cannot be established, refuse to boot: record a scout_signed_out_reason and bounce to /scout/login, mirroring the malformed-payload branch already in main.js:22-37. A force-login that cannot be isolated should fail closed, not degrade into the shared store.

findings.title: Only the four credential keys moved - the remaining per-driver scanner_* state still writes to shared localStorage, so a force-login tab clobbers the real driver's persisted settings
findings.why: persistTripsEnabled(), persistEnabledMapLayers() and the scanner_teammate_overlay_enabled / scanner_enabled_map_layers keys all still call localStorage directly, and forceAuthenticate() invokes both with the force payload. ScoutDriverFlags::for($user, isImpersonating: true) deliberately force-enables the teammate overlay regardless of org config (pinned by ClarityScoutForceLoginControllerTest:183), so opening a force-login tab rewrites the driver's persisted map-layer preferences for that browser profile, and logout() in the force tab wipes them outright (persistEnabledMapLayers([]) plus localStorage.removeItem(ENABLED_MAP_LAYERS_KEY)). map.js also keys its last-known-position cache off the driver id in localStorage (map.js:858-884, 1336). The result is a partially isolated session: identity is per-tab, preferences are not, which is a harder state to reason about than either extreme. plan.md S6 asserts 'all four known readers/writers change together' - the enumeration of four was incomplete because it only counted credential readers.
findings.fix_hint: Either route the scanner_* preference keys through the accessor as well (accepting that a force tab then starts from server defaults, which is arguably correct), or leave them in localStorage but stop writing them from forceAuthenticate()/logout() when isTabScoped(), and say so in the module docblock so the asymmetry is deliberate rather than accidental.

findings.title: Committed public/build assets are stale, so any QA or e2e pass that does not rebuild validates the pre-fix bundle
findings.why: public/build is tracked in git (not ignored - .gitignore only excludes /public/hot and build/phpstan) and the diff does not rebuild it. The committed bundle still contains the pre-fix code: `const t=localStorage.getItem("scanner_token")` in authHeaders, the old handleUnauthorized that does three bare localStorage.removeItem calls, and a main.js entry with no payload validation and no markTabScoped. Production is protected because the image build runs `npx vite build` (Dockerfile:98), but Herd/local runs resolve assets through the committed manifest, so the new Playwright spec and any manual QA step exercising the force-login tab would be testing the old JS unless someone remembers `npm run build`. Combined with finding #2, nothing in the pipeline currently observes the new client code.
findings.fix_hint: Rebuild and commit public/build in this branch (matching whatever convention put it under version control), or add `npm run build` as an explicit precondition in the verification block and the QA plan. Better: stop tracking public/build if the Dockerfile is the only consumer.

findings.title: S2's denied-path audit logging turns an auth-only route into an unauthenticated-by-role activity_log write amplifier
findings.why: The route carries `auth` and nothing else - no policy, no org scoping, no admin gate beyond the session('admin_impersonator') check inside the action. Before this change a request from any authenticated user (including a client-portal or driver account) hit `abort_unless(..., 403)` with zero side effects. Now every such request performs an activity_log INSERT, with kit_id and kit_org_id for a kit the caller may have no relationship to, and route-model binding resolves Kit globally. A bored or scripted authenticated user can enumerate kit ids and write one audit row per request, diluting the very audit trail S2 exists to create and adding unbounded write load to a PostgreSQL table. The 403-before-user-lookup ordering does correctly avoid adding a 404/403 existence oracle, so the disclosure risk is unchanged - the concern is the write path.
findings.fix_hint: Log the denial only when the caller could plausibly be staff (e.g. session has 'impersonator', or the user holds the admin role), or throttle it: rate-limit the route, or de-duplicate denied rows per session/kit within a short window. Alternatively move the denied row behind the same gate that makes the route meaningful and keep a counter/metric for the rest.

findings.title: The deploy hazard the plan says to prove - a mixed legacy + driver-keyed session - is the one shape no test covers
findings.why: plan.md's deploy note says the legacy tolerance 'is what stops their first post-deploy exit from leaving gate-bypassing tokens alive. Prove it with the legacy-shape unit test before release, not after.' The test mints once (producing ['<driverId>' => [id]]) and then Session::put()s a pure flat list, replacing the driver-keyed bucket. The actual post-deploy state is mixed: normalise() folds the in-flight flat list to ['_legacy' => ids] and mintFor() persists it alongside the new numeric driver key, so the session carries both shapes simultaneously. Nothing exercises that: not the mint path over a legacy bucket (does the '_legacy' bucket survive a subsequent mint for a real driver?), not revoke-all across a mixed map, and not the interaction with array_is_list() once a string key is present. The reconciliation logic in mintFor (array_intersect against liveIds) is also only tested for a single driver's own bucket, never with '_legacy' present.
findings.fix_hint: Add a test that seeds a flat list, mints for a real driver, asserts the session now holds both the '_legacy' bucket and the driver key, then revokeTracked() and assert every id from both buckets is gone. Add a second asserting a targeted revokeTracked($driver) leaves the '_legacy' bucket untouched (or deliberately does not, if that is the intent - it is currently unspecified).

residual: exitAdminMode() sends a Filament warning notification but no test asserts it is flashed. Notification::send() pushes onto session('filament.notifications') (vendor/filament/notifications/src/Notification.php:160-162), which does work on a plain redirect, but S3's entire purpose is user-visible feedback for H1 and it is currently unpinned.

exitAdminMode() returns redirect()->back(). On a POST with no referer / no session _previous.url this degrades to '/'. Low impact, but it means the 'silent, no visible change' complaint in H1 is only fixed by the notification, not by the landing page.

okf/concepts/impersonation.md:49 and :56 still document by-name revocation and a GET exit-admin route. plan.md correctly defers this to the post-approval wiki pass per CLAUDE.md; noting so it is not lost.

Kit route-model binding on an auth-only route still lets any authenticated user distinguish an existing kit (403) from a non-existent one (404) across orgs. Pre-existing, unchanged by this diff, and explicitly out of scope per plan.md's rejection of C2.

prune() keeps the newest 3 force tokens per driver globally, not per admin session, so two staff force-logging into the same driver can still prune each other's live token. Pre-existing; the concurrent-mint session-write clobber is acknowledged as deliberately excluded in plan.md.
mintFor() adds one extra SELECT per mint for $liveIds. Irrelevant at 1:1 admin-to-driver request volume; noted only so it is not mistaken for an oversight.

ImpersonateControllerTest::test_exit_admin_mode_get_does_not_revoke_or_clear_admin_mode does not assert a status code, so it pins the effect (no revocation) but not the verb contract (405). It would still pass if someone re-added a GET route that redirected without acting.
unresolved_premises: Whether the Filament 'Login to Scout' action opens force-login in a new tab or navigates the current one. This sets the blast radius for findings #1 and #3: same-tab navigation means the admin's own tab becomes permanently tab-scoped, new-tab means the damage is confined to a disposable tab. Not determinable from the reviewed diff.

Whether the driver's own Scout PWA is ever open in the same browser profile as an admin force-login tab in real operation. Finding #1 is a certainty in the code path; its field severity depends on this. The author's own e2e spec assumes the scenario is real, which is why it is scored High.
Whether QA and the Playwright run rebuild assets. If they do not (finding #6), findings #1-#5 are all unobserved regardless of test quality.

Whether H1/H2/H3 actually explain the 2026-09-16 demo failure. plan.md states attribution is competing-open and that the resolved blocker authorises fixing the root-cause class instead. This review does not revisit that; it reviews the diff against the stated ACs only.

Intended semantics of a targeted revokeTracked($driver) against a '_legacy' bucket. The parameter has no production call site yet, so the behaviour is defined only by the implementation, not by a decision.
